document: The reviewed marathon race registry of this release: every race key with written rows in the adapted input, grouped into races by the rule below and the reviewed joins, flags and labels. `label` is the pipeline’s `city`. analysis/adapt_combined.py rebuilds `races` from the rows it writes and `reviewed`, and stops on any difference; analysis/race_registry.py rebuilds it from an adapted folder.

rule.join: keys join into one race only by the grouping form (HTML entities decoded, accents dropped, lower case, a trailing year or two-digit number dropped, an edition number at the start of the event title dropped with the words edition, edición or edizione, punctuation and runs of spaces made one space) or by a reviewed join; keys that would give a race two editions in one year never join
rule.plain_key: a key with no ": " is a city: its place is the key, its name the race name of its latest edition (the one with most rows when a year has two), its slug the site’s course rule (lower case, accents dropped, other characters to hyphens)
rule.composite_key: place: the part before the first ": ", without parts that are empty, "TBD" or "?", without repeated parts, absent when it is a timing platform’s name (XACT); name: the part after it, HTML entities decoded, a trailing year removed, each word capitalised when the title is all capitals; a race of several keys takes the name and place of the key with its latest edition unless a reviewed join names it
rule.label: unique among the races: a race with a plain key takes that key; a race with a reviewed label takes it (a phrase one of its keys or race names states; the 60 races with most written rows have one, and so has every race with a counted or own-record edition, which the edition policy’s builder checks); every other race takes its name, adding its place in brackets and then its first year where the slugs of two labels would be the same; a plain key’s label and a reviewed label are never changed
rule.slug: a race’s slug is its label under the course rule, so no two races share one and a plain key’s slug is the course page’s

flags.platform_prefix: the part before ": " is a timing platform’s name, so the key states no place
flags.no_marathon_word_in_title: the event title has no marathon word (marat…, 42) once half-marathon words are set aside
flags.other_event_in_title: the event title names another event (half, semi, medio, mezza, 5K, 10K, 21K, relay, ultra, trail, duathlon)
flags.trail_or_mountain_word_in_title: the event title has a trail or mountain word (trail, ecomaratona, sky, mountain, montagna, dolomiti, alpin)
flags.several_race_names: a plain key whose editions carry more than one race name

rule.order: races are sorted by race_id; a race’s keys by first year, then key
